newsitem.title: USA: Firefighters' victory over several U.S. wildfires.
newsitem.headline: Firefighters' victory over several U.S. wildfires.

text.p: Firefighters claimed victory over several major wildfires burning in the western United States on Tuesday but were still battling blazes in eight states.
Cooler weather and rain in some places brought welcome relief to thousands of exhausted firefighters stretched to the limit by the worst fire season in 30 years.
The Boise, Idaho-based National Interagency Fire Centre, which coordinates firefighting efforts, said 19 major fires were still burning, down from 24 on Monday and from a peak of 52 last week.
"We credit it to Mother Nature and an incredible firefighting force that we have out there," said Wendell Peacock, a spokesman for the fire centre.

The fires still burning had consumed almost 330,000 acres (134,000 hectares) in California, Idaho, Montana, Nevada, Oregon, Utah, Washington and Wyoming. More than 13,400 firefighters were battling the blazes.

Intense heat and drought in parts of the western United States this summer have caused fires to spread quickly through parched grass, brush and forest. More than 5.7 million acres (2.3 million hectares) have burned so far this year compared with a five-year average of just more than two million acres (810,000 hectares).

Despite good progress in the last few days, fire weather watches were posted for several areas where gusty winds and low humidity were forecast on Tuesday, creating the conditions for wildfires to spread quickly if they broke out. They included eastern Idaho, western Wyoming, northern Nevada and parts of Oregon and northern California.

Fire officials had feared a new outbreak of fires over the long Labour Day holiday weekend when many campers and hikers visit forests, heightening the risk of accidental blazes. But firefighters quickly put out the few small fires that broke out, averting the danger, officials said.

Only one big, new blaze was reported on Tuesday -- a 635-acre (260-hectare) fire in southwestern Utah. Firefighters contained six blazes, including the 140,500-acre (57,000-hectare) Upper Humboldt Complex of fires in Nevada.

On Monday evening, firefighters fully contained a 21,500-acre (8,700-hectare) arson fire that has burned for a week near Lake Castaic, 60 miles (95 km) north of Los Angeles, said Cliff Johnson, a spokesman for the U.S. Forest Service. Firefighters were still mopping up and improving the line around the fire, he said.

A 625-acre (250-hectare) blaze in the Angeles National Forest in southern California was only half a mile (one km) from the town of Wrightwood, but it posed no immediate threat to the town and no evacuations had been ordered, Johnson said. The fire did force the evacuation of four campgrounds.
With firefighting costs running at about $1 million a day, U.S. Interior Secretary Bruce Babbitt has said he will ask Congress for more money to fight the blazes.
